newsitem.title: USA: Senator optimistic after weekend talks on muni tax.
newsitem.headline: Senator optimistic after weekend talks on muni tax.

text.p: After weekend discussions with Senate Finance Committee aides and other Capitol Hill technical staff, U.S. Sen. Bob Graham is "optimistic" that some of his municipal bond simplification proposals will be approved by the finance panel, a Graham aide said Monday.
Panel chairman Sen. William Roth, R-Del., is expected to circulate a draft of a tax bill on June 17. Committee action is set for June 19.
Graham's aide said that if the senator's provisions are not included in Chairman Roth's draft bill on June 17, Graham will propose them during committee debate two days later.
The aide said Graham will push for approval of only four of the five proposals he circulated for comment last week.
The senator also may focus the four proposals on school construction financing instead of a wider array of bond offerings, the aide said.
One proposal would raise the small issuer rebate exception from $5 million to $25 million, the Graham aide said.

Another would provide a rebate safe-harbor for long-term fixed-rate bonds. Small issuer projects would qualify as long as 15 percent of construction is complete after one year, 40 percent after two years, and 95 percent after three, the aide said.
Graham's plan would increase from $10 million to $25 million the amount of bonds that a government could issue annually which could be purchased by banks.
And the plan would create a new category of exempt activity for educational facilities, the aide to Graham, a Democrat from Florida, said.
Graham has decided not to focus now on modifying depreciation rules to allow tax-exempt financed facilities to receive accelerated depreciation, the aide said.
